[ReZero](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.04887) supports a zero-initialized residual gate. Applied to SASRec, use `h_out = h_base + alpha * recent`, with `alpha=0`, preserving baseline features and logits for finite branch outputs. Algebraically, convex fusion `(1-g)*h_base + g*recent` also preserves baseline at `g=0`, but a finite sigmoid parameter never gives exact zero. Adding normalization after fusion generally changes baseline behavior even at zero gate. Preserve baseline weights, normalization and RNG ordering; initialize new modules after baseline modules. These are implementation deductions from the identity-initialization principle.

[SASRec’s implementation](https://github.com/pmixer/SASRec.pytorch/blob/master/python/model.py) uses a triangular causal mask and computes features for every training position. For the new recent-window branch, permit keys satisfying `sequence[j]!=0` and `max(0,t-W+1)<=j<=t`; zero padded query outputs. Handle empty windows explicitly so masked softmax cannot produce NaNs—multiplying NaN by a zero gate still yields NaN. Keep existing baseline masking unchanged if exact baseline equivalence is required. Cosine support measuring prior evidence for position `t` must instead use strictly earlier keys `j<t`, excluding the diagonal; using `j<=t` introduces trivial self-similarity. Never use a full-sequence summary for earlier training positions.

Efficient implementation deduction: normalize embeddings to `U`, then compute cosine scores with batched matrix multiplication `U @ U.transpose(1,2)`, producing B×L×L rather than B×L×L×D; mask before reduction and aggregate values with another batched multiplication. For fixed-window means, differences of cumulative embedding sums and valid-item counts compute every position in O(BLD). Mean signed prefix cosine support likewise uses `dot(U_t, exclusive_prefix_sum(U))/prior_count`; this shortcut does not apply to clipped, maximum or softmax cosine support.
